Hi Anna — thanks for the agenda. Good catch on the clocks.

Short explanation: the US springs forward on Sun Mar 8 this year, which shifts ET from UTC-5 to UTC-4. Most of Europe (including the Netherlands/UK) doesn't switch until Sun Mar 29. That creates a two-week period where nominal time offsets change — e.g., 10:00 AM ET on Tue is 15:00 in Amsterdam during this window rather than the usual 14:00.

What that means for Tue's demo: if we keep the invite as 10:00 AM Eastern (my calendar), the Amsterdam attendees will see it as 15:00 CET (previously 14:00). I want to make sure that's still acceptable for your engineering team.

Proposed options:
- Keep Tue 10:00 AM ET (which will be 15:00 CET for EU attendees during this two-week mismatch).
- Move to 09:00 AM ET / 14:00 CET to preserve the usual EU local time (a 1-hour earlier start for our east coast folks).
- Offer a recording + a short follow-up session overlapping EU/APAC if the time is inconvenient.

I've attached a quick timezone table and flagged the relevant days. Please let me know which you prefer and we can update the calendar invite.

[attachment: timezone-conversion-table.png]

Thanks — Jordan
